implementation_notes: In .NET the enrichment hook is the messaging framework's pipeline: NServiceBus message mutators (IMutateIncomingMessages/IMutateOutgoingMessages) and MassTransit-style filters run after deserialization and before the handlers, which is where looked-up data or context is merged into the message. The framework owns only the insertion point - the lookup and merge are hand-written - so inject the resource accessor (DbContext, HttpClient, IMemoryCache) into the mutator and keep it unit-testable. Serilog's Enrich.With... pipeline is the same idea applied to log events, which is why 'enricher' is familiar vocabulary in .NET.
pitfalls: A mutator runs for every message of the endpoint, so an uncached lookup there becomes a hidden round trip per message - put IMemoryCache or a hybrid cache in front of the resource.
Replacing context.Message with a different type breaks the handlers' expected contract; enrich the same type (or set properties on it).
An exception in a mutator fails the whole message; a missing lookup must not silently become a poison message unless that is the deliberate policy.

variants.name: Enrich inside the consumer with HttpClient + IMemoryCache
variants.idiom_name: typed HttpClient + IMemoryCache, merge into a record with 'with'
variants.implementation_notes: Without a messaging pipeline to hook (plain queue or HTTP consumer, background service) the enrichment happens at the top of the consumer: resolve the key, read the resource through a typed HttpClient or repository, merge into an immutable record with 'with', and hand the enriched object to the domain logic. IMemoryCache/HybridCache absorbs repeated keys and a resilience policy (timeout, circuit breaker) keeps a dead resource from turning into a dead consumer. Choose it for services that have no framework-provided message pipeline.
pitfalls: GetOrCreateAsync happily caches nulls and failures unless the factory signals them; a resource outage then poisons the cache with the failure for the whole TTL.
Awaiting the resource inside the handler widens its latency budget - pass the cancellation token, set a timeout and define the degraded path.
Records are immutable: discarding the value returned by 'with' silently drops the enrichment, a classic copy-paste bug.
